items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: my Uncle Clay taking me to Old Man Chaloner for lessons. And Old Man Chaloner was a teacher.

ctx.x: They were a lot cheaper then than them now.

Well I got the set and my Uncle Clay taking me to Old Man Chaloner for lessons. And Old Man Chaloner was a teacher. He didn't only teach you. He made you experience of learning to play instruments. He would have a big band of all of his scholars. On Monday you'd go to lessons. On Wednesday all his scholars would be in the band together. So he taking my Uncle Clay to play the bass drum to give the youngsters ideas about a band being so big. So they brought me over and I would play the snare drum. But they had…

items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: I must have went to Chaline about two years.

ctx.x: The person who's playing a drummer. For a time, well, a drummer, he have to keep his time with the bass drum. That's his time, you see. That's his time. Okay, what do you do with the snare drum?
I mean, when you were learning, did you use your foot with Professor Chaline?
Oh yeah, he made you, yeah. You had to, I mean in counting, that's what you mean. Counting to start off and then you pat your feet. You had to, you see.
